datasets_evaluated.evidence: We used the Tranco [11] top 1M list as the top list. The last 30 days were used for the SSLBL [42], while the current list was utilized for the Feodo Tracker [43].

label_source.evidence: A server was labeled a “C2 server” if its IP address was on the Feodo Tracker or the certificate was on the SSLBL.

label_feature_overlap.evidence: We excluded information depending on the current TLS session, a specific server instance, or the TLS certificate.

features_used.evidence: Features are the selected version, cipher suite, received alerts and extension data.

feature_groups.evidence: For each CH, we collect the TLS version, cipher, and TLS extension data from different types of TLS messages to construct the fingerprint.

cert_fields_read.evidence: We excluded information depending on the current TLS session, a specific server instance, or the TLS certificate.

fingerprints_used.evidence: In this work, we propose a methodology based on active measurements to acquire Transport Layer Security (TLS) metadata from servers and leverage it for fingerprinting.

tls_versions_stated.evidence: We only initiate handshakes with TLS versions 1.0 to 1.3 but construct a fingerprint from any version the server sends as a response.

model_family.evidence: This work uses a threshold-based classifier to implement different active TLS fingerprinting use cases.

split_protocols.evidence: It was trained with the data from weeks [1..n] and evaluated using the data from week n + 1.

main_split.evidence: It was trained with the data from weeks [1..n] and evaluated using the data from week n + 1.

shortcut_check.evidence: The Status Request extension was nondeterministic in our measurements (Section V-B); therefore, we removed the extension from the fingerprints, trading the information about the OCSP stapling support of a server for consistency.

metrics.evidence: Well-known classification metrics allow the evaluation of this classifier, particularly precision and recall.

granularity.evidence: In this work, we propose a methodology based on active measurements to acquire Transport Layer Security (TLS) metadata from servers and leverage it for fingerprinting.

first_n_packets.evidence: We generated 10 general-purpose Client Hellos. They served as scanning probes to create an extensive database of TLS configurations to classify servers.
